## Catching a real bug in the knowledge base

`2026-07-09T23:27:26.442Z` · session `02aedcaf` · branch `main`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> ok i see. so the fleek wiki has been consumed by the monorepo vault dwcw. is there anyway to separate for the sake of this case study?

**What came back:**

> Yes, easily. But first let me correct something I said, because I overstated it. I told you a nested vault "breaks the parent's graph view." That was too strong, and I shouldn't have asserted it three times. What's actually true: Obsidian **discourages** nested vaults, and two vaults claiming the same files causes index and config churn. The parent's graph doesn't break — it just absorbs the child…

**What changed because of it:** The Fleek vault had been swallowed by the parent monorepo vault — two Obsidian vaults claiming the same files, each writing its own config. Noticed because the graph view looked wrong, not because anything errored.

## Warning the model that its own context was stale

`2026-07-09T23:59:15.638Z` · session `ba66928b` · branch `fleek-influencer-deck-drafts-353c7d`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> git update please - bare in mind the more recent architectural udpates in other sessionst that have outadted this session

**What changed because of it:** Six worktrees running in parallel means a session can be confidently working from an architecture that another session replaced an hour ago. Managing that staleness is a real skill of working this way, and nobody warns you about it.
